name: Méchoui (roast lamb)
subtitle: Among Moorish nomadic herders in Mauritania, when an animal is slaughtered the best pieces are grilled directly on the embers (meshwiy), while the rest is boiled in a pot.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: When an animal is slaughtered, the best pieces are grilled directly on the embers (meshwiy)

facts.label: Rest of the animal
facts.value: The remaining meat is boiled (metbûkh) in a pot

facts.label: Served to guests
facts.value: For a guest, the best pieces are cooked in the embers or boiled and served as a snack (tajîn) to the guest and the men of the tent

facts.label: Served with
facts.value: The other, boiled pieces come later on a dish of rice or couscous

facts.label: Meaning
facts.value: Slaughtering an animal in a guest's honour is the high point of hospitality practices

facts.label: Custom
facts.value: Keshwa is the gift of a slaughtered animal in honour of a tent that has just settled nearby

facts.label: Festive occasion
facts.value: At the feast ending the pilgrimage to Mecca, a married man is expected to offer a lamb

parts.text: Among Moorish nomadic herders in Mauritania, when an animal is slaughtered the best pieces are grilled directly on the embers (meshwiy), while the rest is boiled in a pot. Slaughtering an animal in a guest's honour is described as the high point of Moorish hospitality.

For a guest, the best pieces are cooked in the embers and served as a first course to the guest and the men of the tent, with boiled meat following on rice or couscous; a lamb is also expected at the feast ending the pilgrimage to Mecca.
